column1: # S6, second format (ZUD): the enemy package decoded, and the object queue's file address widened (state item, old location, new location, size, note)

column2: +0x10, u_long (4 bytes): the file's data address in the heap, or the slot of another loaded object that has it (below 20)
column3: +0x10, 8 bytes (pointer-sized integer, __UINTPTR_TYPE__): the data's address, or the slot (below 20)
column5: the loaders keep reading it as one value; the heap is below 4 GB today, so the values equal the old ones zero-extended (a heap above 4 GB no longer truncates)
the object data queue's slots (vs_battle_objectDataSlots) keep their size and count

column1: ZUD header, battle view zudHeader (146C.c) and menu view _zudData_t (MENU9 592C.c)
column2: the file's 0x30 bytes cast in place, offsets added to the file's address in 32 bits at each use (6 sites)
column3: vs_zud_file (146C.h), filled by vs_zud_decode (146C.c) from the bytes; each part is {pointer into the raw file, size}
column4: 32 on the stack of the caller
column5: both readers call the one decoder; the file stays raw in its heap buffer (allocated and freed by the callers as before), so the game heap's allocation sequence is unchanged; no record is kept (the header is 0x30 bytes, decoded where it is read), so nothing new in the port arena
